title: a crossing made by sail.py's own cross leaves its component's history and state committed, through the ticket machine's published helper
intention: After sail.py's cross lands its own emit (a disposition such as SUPERSEDED, or a FIXME), the crossed component's history.json and state.json are committed, path-limited, by calling the ticket machine's published commit helper.
why: Measured 2026-11-19 on akiendell: five crossings stood only as uncommitted dirt in the house tree until landed by hand on akiendell-1eee-fixme-record (0065e73b6): tester seq 408 (1eeeab70c59e PROVEME->FIXME), codemother seq 172 (35bb99574043 PROVEME->FIXME), verdict seq 32 (8e0cfb77827c PROVEME->FIXME), chart_gate seq 9 (7cae18f7f9c2 TICKETME->BUILDME) and seq 10 (c1a7130fba84 TICKETME->SUPERSEDED). Read: projector.append_entry writes history and state and runs no git; the Stop and PostToolUse hooks in .claude/settings.json commit nothing; the only committer of a crossing's records is close.sh's commit_all, which runs at close or prove, and a verdict refusal or a supersede never reaches it. Law 7: a crossing on one disk is not permanent. RE-PLANNED 2026-11-19 twice: first on the orchestrator's measurement that three of the five crossings came from the gates, then on its RULE 1 ruling that the ticket machine's build is its own ticket (79875eb17ac2) and the clearance gate's is 2955a4a316d3. This ticket keeps the sail.py cross half and calls the machine's published helper.
traces_to: Law 7 (permanent in records of truth); Law 4 (physics, not a hand remembering sail step 10); Law 5 (the repo is itself the state of the machine).
how: A hypothesis, measured by the proof: sail.cross calls cairn.machines.ticket.ticket.commit_crossing_records after its transitions.emit. It depends on ticket 79875eb17ac2 (the helper); until bdd02e0ad010 lets a BUILDME need name a ticket, the dependency is carried here and moves into a stage_needs entry (ticket = 79875eb17ac2) through the door once that gate lands.

clauses.claim: after sail.py cross lands a disposition (SUPERSEDED) or a FIXME in a scratch repo, the component's history.json and state.json are committed and git status of those two paths is clean
another ticket's dirty records in the same tree are not staged or committed by cross

decisions.text: D1: After sail.py's cross lands its own emit (a disposition such as SUPERSEDED, or a FIXME), the crossed component's history.json and state.json are committed, path-limited, by calling the ticket machine's published commit helper.
D2: the red-first proof drives a scratch cross and verdict-to-FIXME, one tooth per clause, PROVES declared.

measured.saw: five crossings (tester seq 408, codemother seq 172, verdict seq 32, chart_gate seq 9 and 10) uncommitted in the akiendell house tree; projector.append_entry has no git call; no Stop/PostToolUse hook commits; close.sh commit_all is the only committer
measured.how: git status and git diff of the house tree on 86cc-red-first-proof, verify_crossing_fingerprint on each entry, grep of projector.py and .claude/settings.json hooks, read of close.sh

measured.saw: the three codemother-actor crossings (1eee, 35bb, 8e0c) were written by chart_gate/gate.py _fail via Ticket.failed (ticket.py:337 emit to FIXME), not by sail.py; sail.py cross (line 218) calls transitions.emit directly; clearance.py:1192 _send_to_fixme is a third emit
measured.how: grep of 'failed at the' (gate.py:257), read of ticket.py passed/failed and sail.py cross, grep of emit callers in clearance.py

measured.saw: the gates' crossings (tester seq 408, codemother seq 172, verdict seq 32, actor codemother) are written by Ticket.failed (ticket.py:337), not sail.py; clearance.py:1164 _send_to_fixme emits directly. Those halves are tickets 79875eb17ac2 and 2955a4a316d3.
